latest_final: The "courses" were not academic classes the student failed to enroll in—they were the food courses of a formal university banquet at HKU, which the student attended as a guest for the evening. At the banquet, serving staff served the dishes and cleared each course away as the meal progressed, after the student had eaten. The opening about choosing courses before the deadline was a deliberate misleading frame: the puzzle plays on the double meaning of "courses." By the end of that one evening, every food course had been served, eaten and taken away by the staff—so all of the student's "courses" were gone in one evening. The event hinged on the student being at a university banquet, staff clearing the courses as standard banquet service, and the wordplay on "courses" rather than any loss of enrolled academic classes.
